terms.definition: The single CairnAdapter object a site declares with defineAdapter (typically in src/theme/cairn.config.ts) and every route factory, admin screen, and delivery helper reads its behavior from.

A documented, stability-tiered point where a site supplies its own code or data to the engine (the content map, render, the access map and roles, identity, custom admin routes, navLayout, BackendProvider), as opposed to engine-internal machinery.
The per-entry `cairn/<concept>/<id>` branch a save commits onto; its existence alone makes the entry pending, and Publish copies it to main and deletes it.

The committed content manifest (src/content/.cairn/index.json): one row per entry with identity, routing facts, links, reference edges, tags, and includes, regenerated and verified at build; distinct from the media manifest.
One of the three places cairn keeps state by what reads it: git (content and both manifests), D1 (auth and operational rows), R2 (media bytes).
The promise an export carries across versions: Extension API and Scaffold API (frozen contracts, a target discipline while cairn is pre-1.0) or Unstable API (no promise across minors).
The @glw907/cairn-cms-dev handle that swaps in-memory fakes for GitHub, AUTH_DB, and the media bucket in a development build, fenced by the __CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__ define and the CAIRN_DEV_BACKEND flag.
The genre-free plumbing under src/chassis/ that every scaffolded site shares regardless of look, reached by a theme only through the $chassis seam.
One of the three layers of Waymark's theme.css tokens, named by how far a re-skin reaches (the daisyUI theme blocks, the owned on-surface floor, and the design scale).
One entry in the adapter's content map: a directory of markdown files plus a fieldset, declared with defineConcept; the set is the site's own.
A concept's declared fields, built from the fifteen field builders, which drive the editor form, the save-time validator, and the inferred TypeScript type.
An entry's markdown filename with .md stripped, its only identity; a dated concept's date prefix feeds only the slug.
A concept's shorthand for its public behavior: feed (routable, dated, in feeds and the sitemap), page (routable, undated, the default), or embedded (no public page).
A fields.reference field that stores another entry's id, typed to one declared concept, recorded as a manifest edge and checked by the build and the admin guards.
An entry of the reserved embedded fragments concept, spliced into another entry's body by `::include{fragment="<id>"}`, one pass deep.
The adapter's one rendering.render function (a SiteRender, usually built with createRenderer) that both the editor preview and every public page call.
A container directive a site registers with defineComponent and defineRegistry, with typed attributes and slots and a synchronous build returning a hast Element.
The public routes and responses a site wires from /delivery and /sveltekit: entry pages, markdown twins, archive, feeds, sitemap, and robots.txt.
A registered component declared with hydrate, whose build() output is the static fallback and which the client mounts over its boundary with hydrateIslands.
The /admin-toolkit set of general-purpose primitives a site's own admin screen composes instead of hand-rolling list, table, and field chrome.
A form action built with createSectionAction, which runs CSRF, identity, access-map authorization, and audit on every call before the site's handler.
The adapter editor group's ordered tree of engine references, site entries, and sections that arranges the admin sidebar; presentation only, never authorization.
The opt-in AI copy-edit an editor triggers on a draft, run through the Anthropic API with the site's model and conventions and checked structurally before review.
A defineAccess declaration keyed by engine screen id or /admin path that narrows, and never widens, which roles reach a target beyond their capability.
A named entry in the site's declared role vocabulary, owner and editor by default, each resolving to one capability.
The floor a role grants: owner, editor, or none (signs in but reaches no engine content).
The IdentityResolver a site passes as createAuthGuard's identity option, whose resolve(event) returns a verified email per request and replaces the whole magic-link path.
A second-audience sign-in built with createAuthChannel: numeric-code request, confirm, and logout actions over the site's own roster and D1 binding, separate from AUTH_DB and locals.cairnEditor.
A revocable, expiring `/preview/<token>` URL minted from an entry's pending draft, where the token alone is the credential.
A media: reference, in body markdown or an image field, that names an uploaded asset by its content hash; the render resolves it through the media manifest to a URL under the public base.
The cairn-audit --rendered run that loads live admin pages in a real browser under a signed-in session and checks what they render, beside the static pass over source files and the compiled sheet.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.job: Learn where cairn ends and your site begins: which export subpath each piece of your site imports, which seams you extend through, where each kind of state lives, and what each tier of the public surface promises across versions. For a Svelte-fluent web developer evaluating cairn against alternatives or taking over a scaffolded site.

exemplars.take: Take the bird's-eye view, then entry points, then a code map with one invariant line per box (what it never does); leave the crate granularity and Rust vocabulary.

exemplars.manifestType: Concept page: architecture explainer ("what runs where")
exemplars.take: Take the follow-one-unit-of-data spine (one edit from save to holding branch to publish to deploy) with guarantees stated at the step that creates them; leave the file-format internals.

pages.figureNote: One diagram of the write path and the three data tiers: an editor save lands on the `cairn/<concept>/<id>` holding branch through the GitHub App, Publish copies it to main, the deploy rebuilds the manifest; D1 and R2 shown beside git with what each holds. Topology only, no branding.
covers: The one-paragraph premise: a site declares one adapter, and every route factory, admin screen, and delivery helper reads its behavior from it.

The export map as six functional groups plus the subpaths outside them (delivery/head, delivery/data, reproductions, log), and the placement rules: nothing on the root barrel imports SvelteKit, nothing on /sveltekit is a .svelte file, no /components subpath; a /sveltekit export bundled outside Vite (a Cron Worker using the audit sink) needs no $app/environment alias.
The three places a site touches the engine (adapter via the root barrel, the SvelteKit layer, the admin mount) and what is engine-internal behind them.

The named seams a site extends through (content map, render, access map and roles, identity, custom admin routes, navLayout, BackendProvider) with one line each and a link to the page that uses it; BackendProvider links its reference entry, since no page builds a second backend.
The write path: save to holding branch, pending entry as branch existence, Publish to main with the editor as author and no committer, the deploy, and the manifest rebuilt and verified at build.
The read path: the admin's batched GitHub reads per entry versus the committed manifest for the content graph.

The three data tiers (git, D1, R2): what each holds, why (placement by what reads it), that no table or manifest row stores an entry body, and that a site's own extension data sits outside them under the cairn_ naming reservation.
Sessions, tokens, audit_log, and preview_tokens as D1 rows, and git history as the edit record (their security properties on security-model).
Cloudflare and SvelteKit as hard dependencies with no host abstraction.

The three stability tiers (Extension, Scaffold, Unstable), that cairn is pre-1.0 so the tiers are a target discipline, and the 0.86.0 navLayout break as the worked example; link to the reference index for per-export tiers.
Commit concurrency: which writes use the head-merge retry and which are head-guarded, publish-all as one commit and one deploy, and the branch cleanup that keeps a concurrent save pending.
The Backend contract behind BackendProvider (expectedHead, missing-path, and missing-branch semantics); signatures stay in the reference.
outOfScope: Declaring the adapter field by field (define-an-adapter-and-schema).
The concept and fieldset model in depth (content-model).
The role column's former database CHECK constraint; state the application-layer check as it is (migration-notes, kept).

pages.title: Add cairn to a SvelteKit app
pages.job: Add cairn to a SvelteKit app, from an empty sv create project or one you already have, through a working /admin on the dev backend to a production deploy that commits through your own GitHub App. For a Svelte-fluent web developer who has Node 24, a GitHub account, and a Cloudflare account.

exemplars.take: Take the objectives stated before any step, the check that ends nearly every step (the page loads at its URL), the "Try it yourself" prompt with its collapsed "Show me the steps." answer, and the closing checklist of "I can" statements before the reader advances; each unit ends live, as each milestone here ends deployed or running; leave the beginner register, the VS Code and Netlify specifics, and the MDX components.
Take the one running example carried through every milestone and the file-location tree before each file's code; leave the appended API reference.

covers: Prerequisites: Node 24, TypeScript 6 pin, a GitHub account, a Cloudflare account, and the Workers Paid plan the moment a second person receives email.

Milestone 1, a bare SvelteKit site deployed: sv create flags, inline kit config in vite.config.ts, adapter-cloudflare named explicitly, minimal wrangler.jsonc, wrangler login and deploy; check: the site answers at its workers.dev address.

Milestone 2, install and wire the engine: the package and its @cloudflare/workers-types peer, ssr.noExternal, the ambient import in app.d.ts, the admin catch-all and layout pair with prerender = false, createCairnAdmin and bootstrapOwner.

Milestone 3, content on disk: the content directories, a minimal adapter, parseSiteConfig, createSiteIndexes and the cairnManifest plugin with their two failure modes (full adapter detail links to define-an-adapter-and-schema); the rendered entry stays unstyled until the site adds Tailwind, daisyUI, and cairn-public.css (link theme-your-public-site).
